newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Firmer on tightening supplies, U.S.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Firmer on tightening supplies, U.S.

text.p: Asian MTBE sellers raised their offer prices this week, amid tightening supplies, the firmer U.S. market and ahead of term negotiations, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"The (Asian) market is tightening up...the U.S. is still volatile but firm and the arbitrage between the U.S. west coast and the Far East is just about open," a producer said.
"It is now a dual market with local and U.S. buyers willing to pay different prices which gives suppliers an opportunity to choose the better outlet and lift price levels," he said.
Sources said the arbitrage to the U.S. west coast would open when free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting in June was priced at $260 per tonne.
The Asian market was now close to that.
Asian buyers, including Thai refiners, were bidding at $255-$257 - around last week's assessed levels of $250-$260.
But one seller said last week he had sold 1,500-tonnes of MTBE lifting in June at $265 fob Singapore.
As a result, sellers' indications edged up from last week, to $260-$265, with one even offering as high as $270, testing the arbitrage window.
"Everybody is finished for June and July," a trader said on market supplies. "To incur cargoes (sales) now is such a liability."
Sellers said they had no or hardly any supplies until August.

The delayed start-up of the 700,000 tonne-per-year Sadaf plant, a joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell and Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC), to mid-July would also keep fresh supplies from coming to the region, sources said.
Suppliers' sentiment was also bullish ahead of renewals of term contracts for the second half of the year, sources said.
"The six-month term buyers have asked for new offers," a source said.

Last Wednesday, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought 7,000-tonnes of MTBE from SABIC for July 6-20 delivery to Kaohsiung or Keelung at $270 per tonne, cost-and-freight, a company official said.
The award was higher than CPC's last tender, for June 10-24 delivery to Italian producer Ecofuel at $267, c-and-f.
"I would look more to the U.S. for direction, or whether suppliers are placing their barrels elsewhere...that is a better indication than CPC's award," a producer said.
